voice: Moving to a new city comes down to one question: where will I actually feel at home? Listings tell you the rent. Commute maps tell you the distance. Ask a chatbot, and everyone gets sent to the same famous neighborhoods. Transplant answers that question with taste.
Tell it a few things you love. Here: Khruangbin, Fleabag, natural wine bars and Aesop. Qloo resolves each one in its taste graph, so Aesop is the skincare brand, not the ancient author.

Then Qloo's heatmaps show where people with this exact mix live across New York. Raw affinity mostly tracks popularity, so Transplant takes popularity out, and ranks neighborhoods by what's left: the taste lift. For this taste, that's Greenpoint.

Every neighborhood shows its evidence: how many Qloo map cells back it, and which parts of your taste drove it. The three picks are kept in genuinely different parts of the city, and if something you love has no signal there, Transplant says so instead of pretending.
Next, your spots. Places Qloo matches to your taste, numbered on the map. And a first week, written only from places Qloo actually returned.

Want somewhere quieter? The guide is a tool-using agent. It searches Qloo's tags, filters places live, and shows every call it made. If Qloo finds nothing, it tells you, rather than inventing a place.
Moving together? Blend two tastes. Transplant ranks by the weaker person's fit, so neither of you is the one compromising, and it shows what you both love.

Twelve cities, for anyone relocating, and for the relocation teams, employers and letting agents who help them. The same engine is also an MCP server, so any AI agent can ask where someone would feel at home. Transplant, powered by Qloo. Try it at transplant-taste dot fly dot dev.
